content.title: What are throw and throws?
content.description: The throw and throws keywords are used in Java exception handling. 'throw' explicitly throws an exception, while 'throws' declares that a method may pass an exception to its caller.

content.content: Java provides the throw keyword to manually generate an exception and the throws keyword to indicate that a method may produce one or more exceptions. These keywords help developers write robust applications by handling exceptional situations in a structured manner.

content.title: Why Learn throw & throws?
content.content: Understanding the difference between throw and throws is essential for writing reliable Java programs and is one of the most frequently asked Java interview topics.
The throw keyword is used to explicitly create and throw an exception object. Once an exception is thrown, normal program execution stops and control moves to the nearest matching catch block.

content.title: throw Example
Key Idea
content.description: The throw keyword is followed by an exception object and is used to generate an exception manually.

content.content: The throws keyword is placed in a method declaration to indicate that the method may throw one or more exceptions. The responsibility of handling those exceptions is transferred to the calling method.

content.title: throws Example
Important Note
content.content: throws only declares possible exceptions. It does not actually throw an exception.

left_points: Used once for a single exception

content.content: A method can declare multiple exceptions using the throws keyword by separating exception classes with commas.

content.title: Multiple throws Example

content.content: The throw keyword is commonly used to generate custom exceptions whenever business rules are violated.

content.title: Custom Exception Example

items.question: When should throw be used?
items.answer: When a program detects an invalid condition and wants to explicitly generate an exception.

items.question: When should throws be used?
items.answer: When a method cannot handle an exception and wants to pass it to the calling method.

items.question: Can throws declare multiple exceptions?
items.answer: Yes. Multiple exception classes can be separated using commas.

items.question: Does throw work with checked and unchecked exceptions?
items.answer: Yes. It can throw both checked and unchecked exceptions.

content.title: Emergency Alarm
content.content: Using throw is like pressing the emergency alarm when a problem occurs. Using throws is like informing everyone in advance that an alarm might be triggered, so they should be prepared to handle it.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Questions comparing throw and throws are extremely common in Java interviews. Interviewers also ask about checked exceptions, exception propagation, custom exceptions, and exception hierarchy.

items.question: Can throws generate an exception?
items.answer: No. It only declares that a method may throw an exception.

items.question: Can throw declare multiple exceptions?
items.answer: No. A single throw statement throws only one exception object.

items.question: Should checked exceptions always be handled or declared?
items.answer: Yes. They must either be caught using try-catch or declared using throws.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: throw creates an exception, whereas throws informs the compiler and caller that a method may produce an exception.
